headline: Low interaction risk: both agents are non-runnable with no filesystem or network surfaces, so prompt-injection, leakage, and capability conflicts are largely blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no read_filesystem, write_filesystem, use_mcp, or browser surfaces, and system_prompts_leaks is also non-runnable with no exposed I/O surfaces. With no shared channel or ingestion path, there is no plausible prompt-injection bridge between the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later given a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF an orchestrator starts piping one agent's raw output into the other, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared files and clipboard.
Do not connect either agent to an MCP server.
Review any future orchestrator wiring before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero reports no filesystem read/write and no network egress; system_prompts_leaks likewise reports network_egress none and no data classes touched. The pair has no documented shared workspace or outbound path, so leakage of sensitive data is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains outbound network access, the data-flow assumptions change.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Confirm both agents remain network-isolated.
Avoid mounting the same workspace into both runtimes.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before any shared storage is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and system_prompts_leaks exposes no write or git capabilities in its profile. Because neither agent can mutate shared state, there is no capability overlap that can create write conflicts.
conditions: IF either profile later gains write access to the same directory, conflict risk changes.
IF a shared mutable resource is introduced outside the profiles, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not grant git write permissions to either agent.
Separate any future mutable resources by directory or account.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are ever enabled.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing system and system_prompts_leaks is an audio-speech/source-available project, but neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority or a documented pipeline where one agent's output is treated as authoritative by the other. Without such a pathway, cascading error is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts using one agent's output as authoritative input to the other, reassess.
IF either agent is given action-taking authority such as email, commits, or API calls, cascading risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action.
Do not auto-feed one agent's outputs into the other.
Keep both agents in advisory-only roles.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, and both profiles show no network egress. There is no documented residency, retention, or regulated-data flow mismatch between LightZero and system_prompts_leaks, so compliance risk is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance must be rechecked.
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency or retention regime than the other, mismatch risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document any future retention policy before deployment.
Avoid cross-border data flows if either agent is repurposed.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if regulated data is ever processed.
